title: Why Does Soap Remove Grease?
topic: Why does soap remove grease and oil when plain water cannot?
claims: Water molecules are polar and do not mix with non-polar grease due to hydrophobic interactions.
Soap molecules possess a polar hydrophilic head and a non-polar hydrophobic tail.
Soap forms micelles around grease, allowing it to be rinsed away by water.
Hot water increases molecular kinetic energy, speeding up the dissolving and melting of fats.

title: How Vaccines Train Your Immune System
topic: How do vaccines actually train your immune system to fight real viruses?
claims: Vaccines deliver a harmless piece or blueprint of the pathogen to stimulate an immune response.
White blood cells detect foreign antigens and produce specific antibodies.
Memory cells store the genetic information required to produce those specific antibodies upon re-exposure.
Booster shots enhance the immune response by reinforcing memory cell populations.

sources.cite: Abayasingam et al. (2021), Cell Reports Medicine. doi:10.1016/j.xcrm.2021.100228
sources.claim: Memory cells store the genetic information required to produce those specific antibodies upon re-exposure.

title: Why Does Baking Soda Fizz With Vinegar
topic: Why does baking soda fizz when mixed with vinegar?
claims: Baking soda is sodium bicarbonate (a base).
The reaction creates sodium acetate, water, and carbon dioxide.
Carbon dioxide gas causes the fizzing.
Unreacted baking soda is basic and bitter.
